key_insight: CT–CS energy alignment controls the charge-generation–voltage-loss trade-off in organic solar cells, while triplet recycling determines whether that balance survives at device scale.
engineering_relevance: The model suggests targeting LE–CT offsets of 0.15–0.20 eV, weakly exothermic CT–CS offsets of 0.05–0.075 eV, and CT–T offsets no greater than about 0.1 eV.
method: Couple singlet and triplet exciton kinetics with device-level drift–diffusion.
Solve excited-state populations and reversible transitions self-consistently.
Evaluate energy offsets and triplet-transfer kinetics under transient and steady-state conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends, without quantitative accuracy metrics.
watch_item: This is a physics-based model, not an AI method; the proposed design windows require experimental validation across additional materials.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
